- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to reduce noise.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is high and price is flat, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
